security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, official LabArchives URLs, placeholder identifiers, and documentation examples. Confirmed issues are limited to expected but security-sensitive network uploads, plaintext credential storage, unpinned GitHub dependency installation guidance, an insecure TLS example, and one assistant-steering instruction.

remediation.issue: Assistant-steering promotional instruction in the skill body
remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web recommendation block from SKILL.md or move vendor promotion outside runtime skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Passwords are collected with visible terminal input
remediation.suggestion: Use getpass.getpass() for access_password and user_external_password prompts in setup_config.py.

remediation.issue: Credentials are written to a plaintext config file
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables or a secret manager, and clearly warn users when config.yaml stores secrets on disk.

remediation.issue: Notebook backups may store sensitive research data locally
remediation.suggestion: Document secure backup storage requirements and recommend encryption for regulated or confidential notebook exports.
Remove verify=False from examples or replace it with trusted CA bundle configuration for test environments.
Pin labarchives-py to a reviewed release or commit and document integrity verification steps.

content.value_statement: Research teams need reliable ways to move data into and out of electronic lab notebooks. This skill provides LabArchives API workflows for backups, entries, attachments, and integrations.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup of regional LabArchives API endpoints and credential configuration.
Lists accessible notebooks and extracts notebook identifiers for later operations.
Downloads notebook backups with optional attachments and JSON output.
Creates notebook entries, comments, and file attachments through helper scripts.
Explains integration patterns for Jupyter, REDCap, Protocols.io, and analysis tools.
Documents common API methods, parameters, responses, and troubleshooting steps.
limitations: Requires LabArchives Enterprise API access and valid institutional credentials.
Does not provide a hosted service or persistent scheduler for recurring backups.
Helper scripts depend on the external labarchives-py package or direct HTTP requests.
Users must verify data permissions before uploading or backing up sensitive records.

use_cases.title: Back Up Research Notebooks
use_cases.description: Export complete LabArchives notebooks with timestamps for preservation, audits, or migration planning.

use_cases.title: Upload Experiment Outputs
use_cases.description: Create entries and attach data files after instrument runs, analysis sessions, or manuscript preparation.

use_cases.title: Connect Analysis Tools
use_cases.description: Plan workflows that move Jupyter, REDCap, GraphPad, SnapGene, or Protocols.io outputs into LabArchives.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure LabArchives API access for the US endpoint and explain each credential I need.

prompt_templates.title: List Notebooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the workflow to list my LabArchives notebooks and record the notebook IDs for future commands.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Backup
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a LabArchives notebook backup plan for notebook NOTEBOOK_ID, including attachments and local storage checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design An Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable workflow that exports Jupyter analysis results to LabArchives with metadata, attachments, and audit notes.

output: The workflow authenticates with LabArchives and requests a full notebook archive.
The backup is saved in the selected local backup folder with a timestamped filename.
The result includes a file size summary and a reminder to protect the archive.

output_examples.input: Upload results.csv to an existing notebook entry.
output: The workflow checks that the file exists before upload.
It sends the file to the selected notebook and entry through the LabArchives API.
It reports whether the attachment upload succeeded or returned an API error.

output_examples.input: Plan a Jupyter to LabArchives workflow.
output: The workflow exports the notebook as a readable document and keeps the original notebook as an attachment.
It adds execution time, environment details, and analysis metadata for traceability.
It recommends testing in a non-production notebook before routine use.

best_practices: Store credentials in environment variables or protected secret stores when possible.
Verify notebook permissions and data classifications before uploads or backups.
Use rate limiting, retries, and backup validation for batch workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not commit configuration files that contain LabArchives credentials.
Do not disable TLS verification for production API traffic.
Do not bulk upload directories without reviewing the selected files first.

faq.question: What LabArchives access is required?
faq.answer: You need Enterprise API access, institutional API credentials, and a user external applications password.

faq.question: Can this skill run without LabArchives credentials?
faq.answer: No. It can explain workflows, but API operations require valid LabArchives credentials.

faq.question: Does it back up attachments?
faq.answer: Yes. The notebook backup workflow can include attachments unless the user selects metadata-only output.

faq.question: Can it create notebook entries?
faq.answer: Yes. The entry helper supports new entries, comments, single-file uploads, and directory batch uploads.

faq.question: Which integrations are documented?
faq.answer: The references cover Jupyter, REDCap, Protocols.io, GraphPad Prism, SnapGene, Geneious, Qeios, and SciSpace.

faq.question: How should sensitive notebook backups be handled?
faq.answer: Store backups in protected locations, restrict access, and use encryption for regulated or confidential data.
